lists.name: Pitchfork: The 200 Best Albums of the 1980s

podcast.body: Released when Sinead was 20, this album was self-produced by her after she fired the initial producer two days into recording, despite being pregnant at the time. The album went gold, received a Grammy nomination, and established her as a strong, independent, and fierce artist of the late 1980s. It contained college and alternative radio hits and was instrumental in building her North American fan base. The title is a line from Psalm 91. "The line in the cobra, the title is a line from Psalm 91, by the way, established Shanade as one of the hottest and most interesting singers of the late 1980s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Sinéad O'Connor's debut album appeared in 1987 and was a sensation. At the age of 20 and seven months pregnant, a situation arising from a relationship with a session drummer, she was astonishingly granted the power to self-facilitate and self-produce this major label release, a level of control rarely afforded to artists her age. "The album was stunning."

podcast.body: This album is regarded as a "stone-cold classic," showcasing Sinéad O'Connor's formidable voice and unique perspective during her early career. "Her first two albums, The Line and the Cobra from 1987, and I do not want what I haven't got from 1990, are stone-cold classics."

podcast.body: Released in 1987, this album led to Sinéad O'Connor being declared "some kind of sensation." She was notably allowed to produce the album herself at the age of 20, a rare opportunity for a new artist on a major label, and it earned her a Grammy nomination. "When her first album The Lion and the Cobra came out in 1987, she was declared to be some kind of sensation with a voice that carried a power and a beauty far beyond her 20 years."
